'''''Aeonium canariense''''' is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Crassulaceae]]. It forms large rosettes of leaves close to the ground but the spikes of yellow flowers stand up to 70 cm tall. It is endemic to the Canary Islands, with five subspecies native to different islands.<ref name = powo/> Subspecies ''canariense'' is native of [[Tenerife]] in the [[Canary Islands]], where it grows on dry slopes and cliffs in the north of the island from sea level to about {{Convert abbreviated|1300|m}}.<ref name=Bramwell>{{cite book|last1=Bramwell|first1=D.|last2=Bramwell|first2=Z.|year=2001|title=Wild flowers of the Canary Islands|publisher=Editorial Rueda|location=Madrid, Spain|ISBN=84-7207-129-4}}</ref>{{rp|162}}

==Subspecies==
Five subspecies are accepted.<ref name = powo/>
*''Aeonium canariense'' subsp. ''canariense'' – Tenerife
*''Aeonium canariense'' subsp. ''christii'' {{small|(Praeger) Bañares}} – [[La Palma]]
*''Aeonium canariense'' subsp. ''latifolium'' {{small|(Burchard) Bañares}} – [[La Gomera]]
*''Aeonium canariense'' subsp. ''longithyrsum'' {{small|(Burchard) Cristini}} – northern [[El Hierro]]
*''Aeonium canariense'' subsp. ''virgineum'' {{small|(Webb ex Christ) Bañares}} – northern and northwestern [[Gran Canaria]]
